sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff: extent bindings; ISA §§3.3, 4.7, 5.1 and 16.2
sol.problem: The diff reads extent parameters from "the caller's resolved region descriptor", but CC/R region calls have no such descriptor. Sections 3.3 and 4.7 pass a qreg and validate its total width against an already known region[A,W]; the ledger contains width, not A and W. Thus the presumed descriptor is not an existing call input. An eight-wire actual can represent region[1,4] or region[2,2]. Those shapes differ operationally: XORing integer 1 into cell 1 of an initially zero register produces flattened value 16 or 4 respectively. The proposed bind metadata identifies which axes to read but supplies neither axis at this boundary. Adding width_args to downstream bindings does not define how this source call supplies them.
sol.fix: Extend §§4.7, 5.1 and 16.2 with an explicit classical call-shape vector, which I recommend: "Each CC/R family call supplies width_args in header parameter order, separately from ordinary args. A wire-bound entry MUST equal the actual operand's ledger width. Memory-axis entries supply A and W; after substitution, every memory actual MUST have exactly 2^A·W wires and satisfy the existing role and disjointness rules. All values are fixed before coherent entry; a mismatch raises FAULT_UB_TRAP before any effect. Nested coherent calls forward shapes from resolved caller declarations." Alternatively introduce typed region(q,A,W) actuals and read the axes from those; that also works but adds a new operand form. The eight-wire example must distinguish width_args ["1","4"] from ["2","2"], yielding 16 versus 4 for the cell-1 operation. Scheduling and estimation requests without register operands must supply the corresponding complete vector explicitly.

sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff: instance bindings; ISA §§9.4, 12.1–12.3
sol.problem: Adding width_args and instance_hash to certificate bindings does not repair the existing certificate record keys. Section 12.3 still permits one regions[closure_hash] record containing one signature and mandatory frame; §9.4 requires literal interface widths after instantiation and permits only c as a frame-expression variable. A fixed root action can invoke the same xor_width family at n=1 and n=3. Both children have the same family closure hash, but their slot widths must respectively be [1,1,4] and [3,3,4]. One existing record cannot satisfy both. The diff neither provides multiple instance records nor defines how claim subjects and inverse-pair references select them. This prevents a conforming certificate for the composed program, despite each instance being individually valid.
sol.fix: Extend §§9.4 and 12.1–12.3, not only the root bindings. Recommended rule: "A concrete width-family certificate region record is keyed by instance_hash and carries closure_hash and width_args. Its signature, bounds, frame and domains are resolved for that instance. Claim subjects, inverse-pair references and composition references distinguish instances; verification for one instance MUST NOT discharge another. A parameter-uniform structural claim may cover multiple widths only by explicitly quantifying them and checking its side conditions throughout that domain." Alternatively retain the family closure key and nest records under instances[instance_hash]; either layout works, but choose one normatively. The mixed-width root must contain two child records with widths [1,1,4] and [3,3,4], and an n=1 claim must not certify n=3.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff, extent bindings; ISA §§3.3, 4.7, 5.1 and 16.2
codex.problem: The diff binds A/W from 'the caller's resolved region descriptor', but that source does not exist at the specified CC/R entry boundary. §4.7 supplies memory slots using qreg operands; §3.3 records a register's total width, not an A/W shape. Existing binding obtains the shape from the literal callee signature. For example, six wires can fill either region[0,6] or region[1,3] in an action. When both dimensions are parameters bound from mem:0, neither the qreg nor the proposed call syntax selects between those shapes. K26 explicitly distinguishes them and forbids inferring shape from total width. The proposal therefore assumes existing entry metadata that the cited contract does not provide.
codex.fix: Amend §§3.3, 4.7, 5.1 and 16.2: 'At a CC/R call, a memory actual whose A or W is parameterised carries an explicit descriptor (q,A,W), with A and W classical unsigned-i64 values or literals. Before any effect, including view consumption, require A≥0, W≥1 and width(q)=2^A·W using mathematical integer arithmetic, then bind the declared extent parameters from that descriptor. Failure is FAULT_UB_TRAP. Coherent callers forward the resolved descriptor of their interface or local region; no shape is inferred from total width.' Thus a six-wire q with (A,W)=(0,6) and the same q with (1,3) select distinct instance bindings. Alternatively, bind extents from explicitly designated classical argument slots and perform the same checks. I recommend the explicit call descriptor, which preserves the separation from ordinary args.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff, instance bindings; ISA §§9.4, 11.1 and 12.1–12.3
codex.problem: Adding width_args and instance_hash to certificate bindings does not resolve the existing certificate representation. §12.3 has exactly one region record per closure_hash, containing one signature and mandatory frame. §9.4 requires slot widths to match the signature and permits only inherited-control count c as a frame-expression variable. Consider outer[n,m] invoking the same family flip[k] on two mutable bundles, forwarding n and m respectively; flip's body is x v[0], valid at every positive width. At n=1,m=3 and c=0, both callees have the same family closure_hash but require mut:0 frame widths 1 and 3. One closure-keyed record cannot represent both, and a single root instance binding cannot identify both child instances. This prevents a conformant composed certificate or launch estimate for a legal use of the extension.
codex.fix: Amend §§9.4 and 12.1–12.3: 'A family region record contains instance records indexed by instance_hash. Each instance record carries width_args, the substituted signature and bounds, and its concrete frame and verification records. Every concrete executable claim and inverse-pair reference identifies the relevant instance. Nested invocation contexts resolve and retain each callee's own width_args and instance_hash; composition distinguishes instance identity in addition to family closure, variant and inherited controls. A width-uniform structural claim must explicitly quantify over all covered admissible width vectors.' In §11.1 require shape context to survive argument/body/template capture and forwarding, as invocation-token context does. The witness must produce two child records, with slot widths 1 and 3 and one forward occurrence each. Alternatively, extend frame/signature expressions and claim quantification to support symbolic family-wide records; I recommend separate concrete instance records as the smaller repair.
